She was gray, dying of cancer, and had refused to let go of the trauma for years.

One inhale through the nose, holding the memory as a contracted ball of energy. One exhale through the mouth, releasing it on command. She broke into sobs — and her color came back in front of the room.

He'd gone to that clinic expecting a spa. Instead he found a ward of people doing everything right with food and still dying, because the thing poisoning them wasn't on their plate.
